areas.name: Russian-occupied Ukraine
areas.note: Crimea (occupied since 2014) and the parts of Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson, Kharkiv and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts held since 2022: about a fifth of Ukraine. Russia claims to have annexed Crimea and four oblasts. Drawn as the Ukrainian municipalities (OpenStreetMap level 3, via geoBoundaries) that are mostly occupied on DeepStateMap's map, so the line is approximate at the scale of individual municipalities.

areas.name: West Bank and East Jerusalem
areas.note: Under Israeli military occupation since 1967; East Jerusalem was annexed by Israel. The Palestinian Authority administers civil affairs in Areas A and B (about 40% of the West Bank).

areas.name: Israeli-held Gaza
areas.note: East of the 'yellow line' set by the October 2025 ceasefire, which Israel has since pushed westward. Israel holds about 63 to 65% of the Strip (64.9% by the UN's count in June 2026, about 63% by Israeli estimates in October) and says it will stay until Hamas disarms. The Strip's outline is from geoBoundaries, which is more accurate here than Natural Earth.

areas.note: West of the yellow line: Gaza City west of Salah al-Din Street, Nuseirat, Deir al-Balah, western Khan Younis and al-Mawasi, about 36% of the Strip. Israel has moved the line west repeatedly since the October 2025 ceasefire. Traced from landmarks in news reports, so expect errors of up to a kilometer.

areas.name: Golan Heights
areas.note: Held by Israel since 1967 and annexed in 1981; the United States recognized the annexation in 2019, but nearly all other states consider it occupied Syrian territory. Includes the Shebaa Farms, claimed by Lebanon.

areas.name: Southern Lebanon
areas.note: Israel has occupied a strip of southern Lebanon since its March 2026 invasion, behind a 'yellow line' about 5 to 15 km deep that includes Khiam and Beaufort Castle, and says it will stay until northern Israel is secure. Traced from the Guardian's 31 May 2026 map; Israel put the area at about 600 km² in August.

areas.name: Syrian buffer zone and Mount Hermon
areas.note: Israeli forces have held the 1974 buffer zone and the Syrian summit of Mount Hermon since December 2024, plus a few positions just beyond it, about 350 km² in all (drawn as the zone plus a 1.5 km margin). US-mediated security talks in 2026 have produced no withdrawal.

areas.note: Run since July 2025 by Druze factions under Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri's National Guard and, since April 2026, his self-declared Jabal Bashan administration. The government holds only villages on the western edge and the eastern desert.

areas.name: Houthi-held Yemen
areas.note: The north and west, home to most of Yemen's population. A Houthi offensive from 3 September 2026 took the Red Sea coast from Hays and al-Khawkhah to Mokha and Dhubab, briefly giving them the whole Yemeni shore of Bab al-Mandab, then cut Taiz city's last road out. A Saudi-backed counteroffensive retook the strait itself on 5 October. The south is held by government and Saudi-backed forces; the separatist STC lost its territory in January 2026.

areas.name: Yemeni front line
areas.note: Districts fought over in October 2026: Dhubab, where government forces hold the strait and airport and the Houthis the north; the mountains west and south of Taiz city, which the Houthis have encircled; the Marib fronts at Madghal and Raghwan; Qa'tabah in al-Dhale; and the populated western edge of Khab wa Ash Sha'f in al-Jawf, split here by eye. Nearly every battlefield claim comes from one side.

areas.name: Eastern and southern Libya
areas.note: Held by Khalifa Haftar's Libyan National Army and the parallel eastern government, including Sirte, Jufra and the Fezzan; the lines have not moved since the 2020 ceasefire. Rivalry in Tripoli is among the western factions, not with Haftar.

areas.note: Almost all of Darfur, where El Fasher fell in October 2025, and all of West Kordofan, where Babanusa's army base fell in December 2025. The RSF also holds ground west and south of El Obeid. Governed by the RSF-led Tasis parallel government.

areas.note: SPLM-North (al-Hilu) has held the core of the Nuba Mountains since 2011. With the RSF it took Kurmuk and Geisan in southern Blue Nile in 2026. Kadugli and Dilling remain army-held, and Kadugli has been besieged again since March 2026.

areas.note: The army retook Bara in July 2026, Sodari town on 25 September and al-Mazroub on 2 October. The RSF still holds Um Badr and Hamrat al-Sheikh in the west of Sodari locality, and El Obeid is close to besieged.

areas.name: Abyei
areas.note: Claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan and patrolled by UN peacekeepers (UNISFA), whose mandate runs to 15 November 2026. South Sudanese forces and RSF checkpoints operate there despite its demilitarized status.

areas.name: AFC/M23-held Kivu
areas.note: Held by AFC/M23, backed by Rwanda, since the capture of Goma (January 2025) and Bukavu (February 2025). Southern Masisi and western Kalehe change hands almost weekly, and Rwanda missed a July 2026 deadline to withdraw its troops.

areas.note: Front-line territories where AFC/M23 holds the eastern or southern parts and the army and Wazalendo militias hold the rest. M23 briefly took Uvira in December 2025, but it returned to the army in January 2026.

areas.note: Has governed itself without recognizing the federal government since 2024, and in August 2026 its forces seized federally aligned bases in Galkayo and Bosaso. It is also fighting Islamic State in the Cal Miskaad mountains. Its edges with Somaliland and SSC-Khatumo are disputed.

areas.name: North Eastern State (SSC-Khatumo)
areas.note: Taken from Somaliland by SSC-Khatumo forces in 2023 and recognized by Mogadishu in 2025 as the North Eastern State, a federal member state aligned with the federal government. Somaliland still claims it, and Puntland disputes parts of Sool and Sanaag.

areas.name: Jubaland
areas.note: Has rejected the federal government's authority since November 2024 and in December 2025 amended its constitution to call itself a government rather than a federal member state. Holds Kismayo, the Lower Juba border towns, and Doolow and (since August 2026) Beled Hawo in Gedo; federal forces hold Garbahaarey and Luuq. Al-Shabaab holds much of the Lower Juba countryside.
